policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'how that by revelation was made known unto me the mystery' opens with an unitalicized conjunction, which renders ὅτι; the base reading begins at κατὰ and leaves nothing for 'how that'.
ASV 'was made known unto me' is passive and subjectless, rendering the aorist passive ἐγνωρίσθη; RP's active ἐγνώρισέν would give 'he made known unto me'.
ASV 'of the promise in Christ Jesus' names Ἰησοῦ and has no possessive on 'promise'; RP's αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ would give 'his promise in Christ'.
ἐγενήθην and ἐγενόμην are the passive and middle aorists of the same verb and person; ASV 'I was made a minister' renders either.

The readings differ only in whether δοθείσης agrees with τῆς χάριτος or δοθεῖσάν with τὴν δωρεάν; ASV 'the gift of that grace of God which was given me' leaves the relative's antecedent open in English.
ASV 'to preach unto the Gentiles' renders the bare dative τοῖς ἔθνεσιν; RP's ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν is locative, which ASV renders 'among the Gentiles' elsewhere (Gal. 1:16).
The readings differ only in the gender and declension of πλοῦτος and its article and adjective; ASV 'the unsearchable riches' is identical either way.
ASV 'to make all men see what is the dispensation' renders πάντας without italics, and its note 'Some ancient authorities read bring to light what is' maps explicitly to the WH omission.
ASV 'God who created all things' ends the clause there; RP's added διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ would give 'created all things by Jesus Christ'.
The readings differ only in the article τῷ before Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ; English drops the article before a proper name, so ASV 'in Christ Jesus' renders either.
ASV 'boldness and access' is anarthrous on the second noun, but English regularly drops a repeated article in a coordinate pair, so it does not show whether RP's τὴν stood in the source.
ἐγκακεῖν and ἐκκακεῖν are orthographic variants of the same verb; ASV 'faint' renders either.
ASV 'I bow my knees unto the Father' stops at πατέρα; RP's added τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ would give 'the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ'.
δῷ and δῴη are alternative aorist forms of δίδωμι in the same person and number; ASV 'that he would grant you' renders either.
The readings differ only in the gender and declension of πλοῦτος and its article; ASV 'the riches of his glory' is identical either way.
ASV 'the breadth and length and height and depth' puts ὕψος before βάθος, matching the base order; the RP order would read 'depth and height'.
ASV 'in the church and in Christ Jesus' has an unitalicized 'and' rendering καί, which RP omits.
